core_summary: Extends place-value knowledge to advanced decimal operations, focusing on decimal multiplication and division. It examines place-value fraction representations (tenths, hundredths, thousandths), establishes place-value division algorithms, explores relationships between dividends, divisors, and quotients (including division by numbers less than 1), and applies decimals to calendar years (Earth's orbit of 365.2422 days) and commercial word problems.
key_concepts: Decimal Place Value System (Tenths 0.1, Hundredths 0.01, Thousandths 0.001)
Multiplication of Decimals using Whole-Number Products and Decimal Place Tracking
Product Behavior when Factors are Between 0 and 1
Division of Decimals via Equivalent Power-of-10 Fractions
Division using Place Value Decomposition (Thousands, Hundreds, Tens, Ones, Tenths)
Dividend, Divisor, and Quotient Dynamics (Quotients exceeding Dividends when Divisor < 1)
Real-World Scientific and Financial Calculations (e.g., Earth revolution 365.2422 days)

key_terms.definition: One part in ten equal parts of a whole (0.1 or 1/10).
One part in one hundred equal parts of a whole (0.01 or 1/100).
Fractions that express the same numerical value or proportion despite different numerators and denominators.
A quotient that includes decimal places resulting from division beyond whole numbers.
The number by which another number (dividend) is divided.
The number or quantity that is divided.

key_takeaways: Multiplying decimals is executed as whole-number multiplication, placing the decimal point according to the sum of factor decimal places.
Dividing a number by a positive decimal less than 1 yields a quotient greater than the original dividend.
Converting decimals into equivalent power-of-10 fractions standardizes complex division into simple whole-number operations.
Precise decimal operations enable modeling astronomical and financial realities accurately.
